Class LatLonSpherical

Namespace
Deodesy.Library
Assembly
Deodesy.Library.dll

Provides functions for spherical geodesy, based on the Haversine formula and other spherical geometry calculations. These functions are adapted from Chris Veness's original JavaScript geodesy library.

AlongTrackDistanceTo(Coordinate, Coordinate, Coordinate)

Calculates the along-track distance from a start point to the point on a great-circle path that is closest to a current point.

public double AlongTrackDistanceTo(Coordinate currentPoint, Coordinate startPoint, Coordinate endPoint)

Parameters

currentPoint Coordinate

The current coordinate.

startPoint Coordinate

The starting coordinate of the great-circle path.

endPoint Coordinate

The ending coordinate of the great-circle path.

Returns

double

The along-track distance in kilometers.

Examples

var start = new Coordinate(53.2611, -0.7972); // N of Lincoln
var end = new Coordinate(48.5734, 7.7161); // Strasbourg
var current = new Coordinate(53.1887, 0.1334); // E of Lincoln
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
double alongTrackDist = geo.AlongTrackDistanceTo(current, start, end);
Console.WriteLine($"Along-track distance: {alongTrackDist:F2} km"); // Output: Along-track distance: 53.7 km

Remarks

This is the distance from the start point to where a perpendicular from the current point crosses the great-circle path.

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if currentPoint, startPoint, or endPoint is null.

CrossTrackDistance(Coordinate, Coordinate, Coordinate)

Calculates the cross-track distance from a current point to a great-circle path defined by two other points.

public double CrossTrackDistance(Coordinate currentPoint, Coordinate startPoint, Coordinate endPoint)

Parameters

currentPoint Coordinate

The current coordinate.

startPoint Coordinate

The starting coordinate of the great-circle path.

endPoint Coordinate

The ending coordinate of the great-circle path.

Returns

double

The cross-track distance in kilometers.

Examples

var start = new Coordinate(53.2611, -0.7972); // N of Lincoln
var end = new Coordinate(48.5734, 7.7161); // Strasbourg
var current = new Coordinate(53.1887, 0.1334); // E of Lincoln
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
double crossTrackDist = geo.CrossTrackDistance(current, start, end);
Console.WriteLine($"Cross-track distance: {crossTrackDist:F2} km"); // Output: Cross-track distance: -31.93 km

Remarks

CrossingParallels(Coordinate, Coordinate, double)

Calculates the pair of meridians at which a great circle defined by two points crosses a given latitude.

public double[]? CrossingParallels(Coordinate startPoint, Coordinate endPoint, double latitude)

Parameters

startPoint Coordinate

The starting coordinate of the great circle.

endPoint Coordinate

The ending coordinate of the great circle.

latitude double

The latitude (in degrees) for which to find the crossing meridians.

Returns

double[]

An array of two doubles representing the longitudes (in degrees, wrapped to -180 to 180) of the crossing points, or null if the great circle does not reach the given latitude.

Examples

var p1 = new Coordinate(0, 0); // Equator, Prime Meridian
var p2 = new Coordinate(30, 90); // 30°N, 90°E
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
double[]? crossingLons = geo.CrossingParallels(p1, p2, 15); // Find where it crosses 15°N
if (crossingLons != null)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Crossing Longitudes at 15°N: {crossingLons[0]:F2}°, {crossingLons[1]:F2}°");
    // Output: Crossing Longitudes at 15°N: 27.65°, 152.35°
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("Great circle does not cross 15°N.");
}

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if startPoint or endPoint is null.

Destination(Coordinate, double, double)

Calculates the destination point and final bearing when traveling along a great circle arc for a given start point, initial bearing, and distance.

public Coordinate Destination(Coordinate startPoint, double distance, double bearing)

Parameters

startPoint Coordinate

The starting coordinate.

distance double

The distance to travel in kilometers.

bearing double

The initial bearing in degrees.

Returns

Coordinate

A Coordinate object representing the destination point.

Examples

var p1 = new Coordinate(51.51, 0.0); // London
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
var destPoint = geo.destination(p1, 7794.0, 300.0); // Travel 7794 km on bearing 300°
Console.WriteLine($"Destination: Lat {destPoint.Latitude:F2}, Lon {destPoint.Longitude:F2}");
// Output: Destination: Lat 34.01, Lon -100.83

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if startPoint is null.

Intermediate(Coordinate, Coordinate, double)

Calculates the point at a given fraction along the great-circle path between two points.

public Coordinate Intermediate(Coordinate startPoint, Coordinate endPoint, double fraction)

Parameters

startPoint Coordinate

The starting coordinate.

endPoint Coordinate

The ending coordinate.

fraction double

The fraction along the path (0.0 for startPoint, 1.0 for endPoint, 0.5 for midpoint).

Returns

Coordinate

A Coordinate object representing the intermediate point.

Examples

var p1 = new Coordinate(51.51, 0.0); // London
var p2 = new Coordinate(38.89, -77.03); // Washington D.C.
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
var intermediatePoint = geo.Intermediate(p1, p2, 0.25); // 25% of the way
Console.WriteLine($"Intermediate Point (25%): Lat {intermediatePoint.Latitude:F2}, Lon {intermediatePoint.Longitude:F2}");
// Output: Intermediate Point (25%): Lat 53.82, Lon -21.65

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if startPoint or endPoint is null.

Intersection(Coordinate, double, Coordinate, double)

Calculates the point of intersection of two great-circle paths.

public Coordinate? Intersection(Coordinate firstPoint, double firstBearing, Coordinate secondPoint, double secondBearing)

Parameters

firstPoint Coordinate

The starting point of the first path.

firstBearing double

The initial bearing of the first path in degrees.

secondPoint Coordinate

The starting point of the second path.

secondBearing double

The initial bearing of the second path in degrees.

Returns

Coordinate

A Coordinate object representing the intersection point, or null if no intersection or paths are coincident.

Examples

var p1 = new Coordinate(51.8853, 0.235); // Cambridge
var brng1 = 108.549; // Bearing from Cambridge
var p2 = new Coordinate(49.0034, 2.5735); // Paris
var brng2 = 32.435; // Bearing from Paris
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
var intersection = geo.Intersection(p1, brng1, p2, brng2);
if (intersection != null)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Intersection: Lat {intersection.Latitude:F2}, Lon {intersection.Longitude:F2}");
    // Output: Intersection: Lat 50.99, Lon 4.50 (near Brussels)
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("No intersection found.");
}

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if firstPoint or secondPoint is null.

MaxLatitude(Coordinate, double)

Calculates the maximum latitude reached when traveling on a great circle from a start point with a given initial bearing (using Clairaut’s formula).

public double MaxLatitude(Coordinate startPoint, double bearing)

Parameters

startPoint Coordinate

The starting coordinate.

bearing double

The initial bearing in degrees.

Returns

double

The maximum latitude in degrees.

Examples

var p1 = new Coordinate(51.51, 0.0); // London
var geo = new LatLonSpherical();
double maxLat = geo.MaxLatitude(p1, 90.0); // Bearing East
Console.WriteLine($"Max Latitude: {maxLat:F2}°"); // Output: Max Latitude: 51.51°

Remarks

The maximum latitude is independent of longitude; it will be the same for all points on a given latitude. Negate the result for the minimum latitude (in the Southern Hemisphere).

Exceptions

ArgumentNullException

Thrown if startPoint is null.
